rationale: ROUND 2 on correlation 9521d62f — every round-1 objection measured or answered; the implemented state (not a sketch) is what is under review, and the sketches below now show the shipped hunks verbatim. THE ORIGINAL CASE (unchanged): bugs_open/134 — the documentation convention for 'optional' (a trailing '?') leaked from seed 156's own comment into two real JSON config key names, so product-spec-refresher's refresh_specs step carried "category?" and "limit?" while the action reads category and limit; neither key ever resolved and nothing said so. Fix is three-part: correct the data at both sources (seed 156 + live row via migration 298), opt the action into the SCR-003 contract (CheckConfig: true), and close the class with config-key-audit --suspicious-keys (doc-notation punctuation in any live step-config key, fleet-wide, independent of opt-in). ROUND-1 OBJECTIONS, ANSWERED: (1) editquality HIGH, snapshot overload — measured both ways: pg_get_functiondef shows snapshot_agent(text) INSERTs INTO agent_definitions (is_snapshot row) while the two-arg form used by 298 INSERTs INTO agent_definitions_backup; and at the artefact, the applied migration's snapshot row IS in agent_definitions_backup (snapshot_taken_at 2026-08-03 11:06:17Z, reason naming the file) with the old 'category?' key preserved in its stored config — the restore target genuinely holds the pre-update state. Zero is_snapshot=true rows for this type in agent_definitions. The migration's rollback comment now records this, including 'order by snapshot_taken_at, never created_at' (agent_definitions_backup keeps the source row's id/created_at). (2) editquality MEDIUM, pending-file/--apply exposure — 298 was applied by hand (snapshot, UPDATE 1, both DO/RAISE verify blocks passed, COMMIT clean) and registered in the ledger via run-migrations.sh --record-only BEFORE this commit, so it is not pending and the next --apply cannot take it; it is also fenced on the bad key's presence, so even a rogue replay is a no-op. It is not ordering-critical (no Go dependency in either direction), so the _HOLD.sql convention does not apply. (3) tooling_provenance — the doc_notes row landed: measured post-apply, created_at 11:06:17Z, subject_type 'pipeline', categories ["migration"], matching the 296 precedent row shape. (4) guardian, vocabulary — edit 3's operation is now labelled config_change: the file is new but the effect is a live agent_definitions.default_config mutation, single agent type, and the blast radius argument is stated in those terms. (5) guardian, script exit-1 consumers — two facts: tree-wide grep for 'audit-config-keys' finds only comments (no CI, no makefile, no cron caller — the tool's own header records the same check), AND the script already exits 1 on today's fleet regardless of this change (three pre-existing unknown-key actions: plan_sections domain, run_discovery_checks check_domain, triage_detected_items target_domain — the bug-136 family, deliberately not touched by this lane), so no consumer keyed on exit-0 can exist in practice. (6) debug_historian, post-roll verification — stated honestly: CheckConfig: true is a bool field flip and contributes NO compiled string literal, so a strings-grep of the chassis binary cannot discriminate it (the recorded 2026-08-03 WRONG_CALLS row about pod-grepping for comments is exactly this trap); the offline halves are already proven LIVE from HEAD source — the report was run against the live fleet BEFORE the migration (both new detections fired: this agent under UNKNOWN KEYS via CheckConfig, both rows under SUSPICIOUS KEYS, exit 1) and AFTER it (SUSPICIOUS KEYS none, agent gone from UNKNOWN KEYS) — which is an induced-fault verification of the whole detection pipeline; the runtime validator arm is belt-and-braces on top, and inducing its warning post-roll would mean dispatching a Firecrawl-scraping agent with a junk key, which is declared not worth the run. The lane's NOTES record this commitment and its stated limit. (7) debug_historian, redundant #- chain — the round-1 SKETCH was redundant; the shipped SQL is the single clean form (subtract the two keys from the extracted object, merge the corrected pair, one jsonb_set) and edit 3's sketch below is now the shipped hunk. (8) prior_art_librarian, '0 runs ever' — CORRECT, RETRACTED, and logged in WRONG_CALLS.md 2026-08-03: orchestration_states is retention-clocked and supports 'none within retention', never 'none ever'; follow-up measurement found 10 products carrying the verified_date stamp the action writes — one dated 2026-07-14 (predates the agent: hand-written) and five dated 2026-07-22, consistent with a reaped manual run. The safety argument no longer rests on run count: the bad keys never resolved, so ANY historical run necessarily behaved as the defaults (category 'gripper', limit 20); a caller passing nothing gets byte-identical behaviour after the fix; the only behavioural delta is that a future caller explicitly passing category/limit is honoured instead of silently ignored — which is the seed's own documented contract, and the silently-ignored case is itself the defect. scheduled_tasks = 0 for this agent (a table with no reaper), so no automated caller exists. (9) guardian/prior_art_librarian, precedent citation — the 'two seats objected to a second binary' precedent is quoted verbatim in cmd/config-key-audit/main.go's own header (2026-07-28, corr 07cf67c6), and round 1's own reviewer checks surfaced the 2026-07-28 council round confirming it.

New file, but the EFFECT is a live agent_definitions.default_config mutation on one agent type, so it is labelled by its effect per the round-1 guardian objection. edits.sketch:
BEGIN;
SELECT snapshot_agent('product-spec-refresher',
    '298_fix_product_spec_refresher_optional_marker_keys.sql: pre-update');
-- One write, not two. The object is rebuilt by subtracting both marker keys and
-- merging the corrected pair back in, so a partially-applied state (one key
-- renamed, one not) is not representable.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(
      default_config,
      '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}',
      ((default_config #> '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}')
         - 'category?' - 'limit?')
        || jsonb_build_object(
             'category', 'input_data.category',
             'limit',    'input_data.limit'),
      false)
WHERE type = 'product-spec-refresher'
  AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot, false) = false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config #> '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}' ? 'category?';
-- doc_notes INSERT (pipeline/build, ["migration"], 296's shape) — landed, measured.
-- Then two DO/RAISE blocks: (1) category+limit correct AND marker keys gone;
-- (2) site_id neighbour intact AND sibling steps ensure_site_record/complete
-- survive. COMMIT. Trailing comments: verify query, fleet-wide re-check SQL,
-- and the rollback story naming agent_definitions_backup + order by
-- snapshot_taken_at (the backup keeps the source row's id/created_at).

edits.rationale: Close the class, not the instance. CheckConfig only protects opted-in actions; this defect lived on an action outside that population for six weeks. A top-level step-config key containing '?', '*', a space or ':' is schema-doc punctuation and never a readable key for ANY action, so it is reportable without the action's opt-in. Same house pattern as --unregistered-actions: a flag on this binary (the 07-28 two-seats precedent against second binaries, quoted in this file's own header), pure function + fixture tests, same stdin export, walked with validation.WalkSteps so nested sub-workflow steps are covered (bugs_open/144), refuses an empty decode with exit 2, exit 1 on findings. The character set is deliberately narrow — every character is one that cannot plausibly appear in a key an action reads, so a finding is always signal; a broader set becomes a linter people learn to ignore.

Five fixture tests: the live refresh_specs step exactly as bug 134 found it (both marker keys flagged, clean site_id neighbour not); the other three characters each on their own fixture; a marker key inside a loop sub-workflow flagged with Nested=true and the full path (asserts the WalkSteps traversal — the bugs_open/144 arm — so a regression to a top-level range fails a test rather than going quietly blind); a negative control over ordinary keys (site_id, a.b, max_pages, upload-result, input_fields) including the []-not-null encoding; and a 20-iteration determinism test (Go randomises map iteration, so an unsorted implementation fails it rather than passing by luck). Mutation-proven: with the ContainsAny check neutered, three of the five fail loudly; restored, all pass with -count=1.

The report is where sessions already look; the fourth section runs whenever the coverage report runs, against the WORKFLOWS_JSON the script already fetched — one traversal implementation, the tested Go one, not a second SQL walk. Exit semantics: 1 if unknown keys OR suspicious keys (both are real inert-key defects, unlike the undeclared-actions coverage gap); the empty-stdout refusal path exits 2. Verified live pre-migration (both detections fired, exit 1) and post-migration (suspicious none; residual exit 1 is the three pre-existing bug-136-family unknown keys, deliberately untouched). One trap found and recorded in the script comment: `go run` collapses the child's exit status (a 2 becomes 1), so the refusal discriminator is empty stdout — the same pattern DECLARED and LIVE already use — not the code.
edits.sketch:
SUSPICIOUS="$(printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS_JSON" | (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --suspicious-keys))"
SUSPICIOUS_RC=$?
if [[ -z "$SUSPICIOUS" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: the suspicious-key check printed nothing (rc $SUSPICIOUS_RC) — it refuses to" >&2
    echo "       report over an empty or broken export rather than printing a clean one" >&2
    exit 2
fi
# passed into the existing python heredoc as an env var (same pattern as DECLARED/LIVE);
# text mode prints '=== SUSPICIOUS KEYS (…) ===' with 'agent path action.key (nested)' rows or 'none';
# --json gains "suspicious_keys"; final line becomes:
sys.exit(1 if (unknown_by_action or suspicious) else 0)

plan.risks: 1) The live-row mutation is done and artefact-verified; residual risk is now the rollback story, which is proven at the artefact (backup row read back, old keys present) rather than assumed. 2) Behaviour change: a future caller explicitly passing category/limit is honoured instead of silently ignored — the seed's documented intent; a caller passing nothing sees byte-identical behaviour; any historical run necessarily behaved as defaults because the bad keys could not resolve. 3) The suspicious-key character set is deliberately only ?/*/space/colon; a doc convention using other punctuation would pass — judged acceptable because every widening trades signal for noise, and the set matches the only convention observed in this estate. 4) scripts/audit-config-keys.sh exit-1 surface: no automated caller exists (grep, plus the tool header's own record of that check), and the script already exits 1 on today's fleet for the three pre-existing bug-136-family unknown keys, so no consumer keyed on exit-0 can exist in practice. 5) CheckConfig arms the runtime validator only after the next chassis roll; it is a bool with no compiled string marker, so post-roll pod verification cannot use a strings-grep — the offline report (proven live from HEAD source, both directions) is the primary detector and the runtime warning is belt-and-braces; this limit is stated in the lane's NOTES rather than left implicit.
